limitations: The exact transaction is canonical, but the original negotiation chat has not been recovered.
Robert's current recollection is unusually specific about the objective and quarterback decision, but it is still a 2026 reconstruction rather than contemporaneous documentation.
The later player outcomes of Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, CeeDee Lamb, Jahmyr Gibbs, Marvin Harrison Jr., Jordan Love and Rome Odunze are excluded from the ex-ante reconstruction.
Numeric outcome uncertainty and decision margin remain open pending explicit user calibration before sealing.

evidence_basis.note: Confirms the completed startup position swap and exact original pick assets.

Robert remembers the trade objective very clearly: secure a long-term dynasty quarterback anchor so he would not need to keep solving QB. His intended elite-QB set was Patrick Mahomes or Josh Allen. He was highly confident in the trade-up concept, while the later Mahomes-versus-Allen selection itself felt materially less certain.

Robert recalls preferring Mahomes after acquiring 1.01 because Mahomes felt like the safer established dynasty bank; Allen offered clear rushing upside but Robert had concerns about the durability/sustainability of the rushing style and whether Allen would fully establish himself at that level. This is a draft-selection rationale nested inside, but distinct from, the trade-up decision.

decision_context.objective: Move from startup 1.02 to 1.01 so Robert could lock in a long-term elite dynasty quarterback anchor and reduce future QB decision burden.
decision_context.roster_context: This was the startup draft in the league's original one-quarterback setting. Robert wanted to establish the most important long-term quarterback slot immediately rather than revisit the position repeatedly.
decision_context.cap_salary_context: No salary/cap system was part of Robert's recalled rationale for this startup trade.
decision_context.team_window: The league was at dynasty inception, so the objective was foundational multi-year roster construction rather than a short contender/rebuild window.
decision_context.market_context: Robert's remembered elite target set was Patrick Mahomes or Josh Allen. After the trade, the actual 1.01 selection decision remained close between those two even though Robert was much more confident in the trade-up objective itself.
decision_context.why_now: The startup 1.01 was the point at which Robert could control the elite quarterback choice and establish a long-term franchise anchor.
constraints: The trade exchanged Robert's original 1.02/2.05/6.05 positions for Tim's 1.01/2.06/6.06 positions, so control of 1.01 came with small position losses later in the startup.
Robert wanted an elite long-term quarterback more than he wanted to preserve the slightly earlier later-round positions.

theses.statement: In a dynasty startup, securing control of the top quarterback choice was worth small later-round position concessions because an elite long-term QB would stabilize the roster for years.
falsification_conditions: The elite quarterback tier did not provide meaningful long-term stability relative to remaining at 1.02.
The later-round position concessions materially outweighed the value of controlling the quarterback choice.

theses.statement: Mahomes and Josh Allen formed Robert's acceptable elite-QB target set, but the trade decision was stronger and more certain than the subsequent choice between those two players.
falsification_conditions: Robert would not actually have been comfortable building around either quarterback.
The trade-up was only valuable if one specific quarterback, rather than the elite-QB tier, was available.

alternatives.description: Remain at startup 1.02 rather than swapping positions with Tim.
alternatives.reason_not_chosen: Robert's recalled priority was to secure control of the elite long-term quarterback decision rather than accept less control at 1.02.

price_ceiling.description: Robert remembers being confident that the move-up was worth doing, but does not currently recall a separate pre-defined maximum price beyond the executed position swap.

known_risks.description: The trade paid for control at 1.01 even though Robert's acceptable quarterback set contained both Mahomes and Josh Allen.
The value of the trade depended on an elite quarterback anchor actually providing the long-term positional stability Robert expected.

decision_state_at_execution.confidence_rationale: Robert recalls being clearly in favor of the trade-up and highly confident that securing an elite dynasty quarterback anchor was strategically important. His uncertainty was concentrated much more in the Mahomes-versus-Allen player choice than in the trade-up itself.
decision_state_at_execution.primary_confidence_driver: Long-term positional stability: acquire an elite quarterback and avoid repeatedly solving the position.
decision_state_at_execution.primary_source_of_doubt: The exact Mahomes-versus-Allen choice remained close; Robert questioned whether choosing the safer Mahomes profile over Allen's rushing upside was correct.
known_personal_biases: Preference for long-term positional security and the safer established quarterback profile over the more volatile rushing-upside profile.
